comparator.name: Communication and Information Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Dutch target, September-2026 curriculum with Business Communication retained as first-listed on the public theme page, independently of UCR fit. The adopted TSHD appendix explicitly gives 2027–2028 and 2028–2029 upper years. The public page and adopted appendix order themes differently; their listed Business Communication requirements agree. Common first-year study is 60 EC. Year 2 combines 30 common EC, 24 theme EC and six restricted elective EC: Content Marketing and Analytics is the first permitted non-duplicated choice. Year 3 retains thirty approved exchange credits, eighteen restricted credits as Persuasive Design, Creativity and Cognition and Misinformation and Polarization, and the twelve-credit literature-review thesis. These are the first three non-duplicated Spring choices in the adopted menu after the year-two subjects. No internship, second complete theme or named host is imposed. Thesis entry requires 120 credits including the six specified language and methods subjects. The ordinary first two years complete those requirements. Zero-credit GROW and participation in the first-year subject pool are separate from credit totals. Future new subjects have public descriptions and adopted places; the 2026 catalogue explicitly defers their fuller course information to 2027–2028, so no unlisted outcomes are inferred.

components.name: Communication and Information Sciences in Practice
Research Seminar 3: Content Analysis
components.note: The research seminar collects and analyses language corpora, including manual and automated annotation, and reports a quantitative content analysis.

components.name: Content Marketing and Analytics
components.note: Selected from the restricted second-year elective list. Content Marketing and Analytics is not repeated among the third-year choices.

components.name: Exchange / Study Abroad
components.note: Thirty credits remain reserved for approved partner-university study. No destination or course package is imposed. The package must satisfy academic level, non-overlap and entry requirements.

components.name: Persuasive Design
components.note: Selected from the third-year restricted menu. It develops and evaluates a persuasive interaction design using psychological theory and user data.

components.name: Creativity and Cognition
components.note: Selected as a second distinct third-year elective, studying cognitive processes and theories of creativity.

components.name: Misinformation and Polarization
components.note: Selected as a third distinct third-year elective. Together these choices fill eighteen credits outside the completed Business Communication theme.

components.name: Bachelorthesis
components.note: The twelve-credit thesis independently answers a communication-science question through a systematic literature review. Entry requires 120 programme credits including Academic Dutch, Academic English, Methodology, Statistics, Survey & Interview and Experiment. A proposal is assessed before the review and final report; an oral check follows.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target names no theme. Business Communication is first-listed in the current public programme theme descriptions, so that independently neutral tie-break is retained. The adopted appendix lists themes in another order but confirms the same selected route. The required restricted selections are instantiated from the first non-duplicated permitted Spring options; thirty exchange credits remain genuinely open.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad route covers communication theory, organisations, media, persuasion and research. Social-impact communication and human/digital communication have independently evidenced organising logics and materially different course selections. The optional Dutch-language teacher-preparation route is a further stable direction, but no fourth programme can be included.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop research-based academic writing, structured argument, source use and presentation. Tilburg specifically teaches English register, grammar and mechanics; UCR combines these academic-writing functions with personal development and civic engagement.
Both develop brands, marketing communication and consumer engagement using audience evidence and responsible strategy. The selected tools and project contexts differ.

Both teach measurement, research design, surveys, experiments, reliability, validity and ethics. UCR additionally conducts an empirical team project; Tilburg applies the framework specifically to communication research.

Both investigate communication within groups and organisations. UCR centres leadership communication, ethical influence and a leader’s communication challenge; Tilburg teaches wider collaboration and organisational-communication theory.

Both address employee motivation, teams, leadership, power, culture and organisational change. UCR provides organisational-psychology evidence; Tilburg specifically investigates communication channels, employee voice and an internal communication audit.

Both examine ethical and social questions about AI, autonomy and human interaction. Tilburg centres media society, public space, ideology and algorithmic bias; UCR combines AI ethics with psychological, organisational and care relationships.

Both introduce Python, variables, loops, functions, data formats and debugging. UCR also develops recursion and object-oriented programming; Tilburg emphasises communication-related text and data applications.

Both examine the nature of thinking and effects of technology on minds through philosophical arguments. Tilburg additionally covers philosophy of science and ethics; UCR centres mind, consciousness and experience.
Both design, conduct and report human-subject research through interviews. UCR emphasises qualitative methods and interpretation, while Tilburg also carries out and analyses survey research.

Both investigate cognition such as attention, memory, emotion and control using empirical studies. UCR centres neural mechanisms and a cognitive experiment; Tilburg connects cognitive findings more broadly to communication.

Both select, conduct and interpret statistical analyses of human data, including group comparisons and relationships, and report results. UCR adds experimental-design and multivariable modelling; Tilburg teaches the introductory communication-statistics workflow.

Both analyse communication through theoretical models, including rhetoric and influence. UCR concentrates on classical rhetoric, argument and public speech; Tilburg also covers interpersonal relations, media effects and active audiences.

Both apply communication knowledge to a real social challenge with an external partner. UCR centres rhetorical education and public speaking with local schoolchildren; Tilburg develops a communication strategy and conceptual plan.

Both study persuasive strategies, attitudes and behaviour and apply them to messages for a specific audience. UCR develops community communication about sustainable lifestyles; Tilburg surveys persuasion theories and message design.

Organisational psychology, persuasion and business governance contribute related perspectives, but no selected course provides the dedicated stakeholder, reputation, crisis and strategic-communication sequence.
AI ethics, programming, neural models and organisational transformation supply separate foundations, not a dedicated course on generative conversational technology in organisational communication.
The selected Content Marketing and Analytics elective joins content strategy and audience-oriented data analysis. No selected UCR course supplies that combined specialism.
Thirty credits remain open for approved exchange study; no host or course package is invented.
Persuasion and psychology supply relevant concepts, but no selected UCR course centres iterative persuasive interaction design and evaluation using user data.
Creative practice and cognitive science contribute in different courses, but none is counted again as the dedicated psychology-of-creativity elective.
Social theory, media analysis and ethics inform public debate, but no selected course supplies this dedicated misinformation and polarisation elective.
The individual communication-science systematic literature-review thesis remains a separate requirement. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.
